question.text: A car of mass ' $m$ ' moves on a banked road having radius ' $r$ ' and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is

solution.text: So, $N=m g \cos \theta+\frac{m v_0^2}{r} \sin \theta$ $f_r=\mu m g \cos \theta+\frac{\mu m v_0^2}{r} \sin \theta$ $\begin{aligned} & \text { And } \frac{m v_0^2}{r} \cos \theta=m g \sin \theta+f_r \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{m v_0^2}{r} \cos \theta-m g \sin \theta=\mu\left(m g \cos \theta+\frac{m v_0^2}{r} \sin \theta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left(v_0^2-g r \tan \theta\right)=\mu\left(v_0^2 \tan \theta+g r\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mu=\frac{v_0^2-g r \tan \theta}{g r+v_0^2 \tan \theta} \end{aligned}$
